title: Workplace Equity & Accessibility Guide — Reasonable Accommodations, Benefits, and Onboarding
author: Sofia Alvarez
content:
Summary:

This guide defines Redwood’s approach to workplace equity and accessibility across hiring, onboarding, benefits, role progression, and internal tooling. It explains how to request reasonable accommodations, how benefits and perks can be adapted, and how managers and People Ops collaborate to ensure equitable outcomes for all contributors.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and interns globally (subject to local law and country-specific benefits).
- Covers accommodation requests for interview/hiring, first‑day onboarding, recurring workplace needs, event accessibility, and long‑term adjustments tied to disability, caregiving, religious needs, or neurodiversity.

Principles:
1. Respect and dignity: requests are handled with confidentiality and a focus on participant comfort.
2. Timely response: People Ops or an assigned intake owner acknowledges requests within 48 business hours.
3. Reasonable and individualized: accommodations are assessed case-by-case with a preference for practical, low-friction solutions.
4. Iterative improvement: we monitor outcomes and update policies, tooling, and benefits to close gaps.

Key definitions:
- Reasonable accommodation: a change to the workplace, schedule, benefits, or tools that enables a contributor to perform essential job responsibilities.
- Interactive process: a conversation between the employee, manager, and People Ops to identify effective accommodations.

Accommodation intake and decision process (step-by-step):
1. Request initiation:
   - Employee fills the Accommodation Request Form (link at the end) or emails accommodations@redwood.com; self‑identified requests via managers are acceptable.
2. Acknowledgement (SLO):
   - People Ops assigns an intake owner and acknowledges receipt within 48 business hours.
3. Information gathering (3–7 business days typical):
   - Intake owner collects basic context (impact on tasks, preferred adjustments). Medical documentation is not required for initial requests; if needed for complex long‑term provisions, People Ops will explain why in writing and keep documents secure.
4. Interactive assessment (7–14 business days typical):
   - Manager + People Ops propose 1–2 trial accommodations; vendor quote requests (e.g., assistive tech) are initiated if required.
5. Implementation and trial (2–30 days):
   - Implement chosen adjustments and evaluate at 2-week and 8-week checkpoints. Adjust as needed.
6. Ongoing review:
   - Annual check-ins or sooner if circumstances change.

Table: common accommodations catalog (summary)

| Accommodation type               | Typical lead time | Owner / helper                | Notes / examples                                           |
|---------------------------------|-------------------:|-------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| Flexible schedule / core hours  | 1–3 days           | Hiring manager + People Ops   | Shifted core hours, compressed workweek                    |
| Remote-first assignment         | 2–7 days           | Manager + People Ops           | Permanent or hybrid remote arrangements                     |
| Assistive software / settings   | 1–14 days          | IT / IT Access team            | Screen readers, high-contrast themes, font scaling         |
| Ergonomic equipment             | 3–14 days          | Facilities / Procurement       | Standing desks, ergonomic chairs, keyboard adapters       |
| Quiet workspace / private room  | 1–7 days           | Facilities / Workplace ops     | Bookable quiet rooms, noise‑reducing partitions            |
| Extra onboarding time / buddy   | 1–3 days           | Hiring manager + Onboarding    | Extended ramp schedule, dedicated peer mentor             |
| Event accessibility             | 7–30 days          | Events + People Ops            | Captioning, ASL interpreters, virtual participation option|

Onboarding: inclusive first 90 days
- Pre-start checklist (People Ops):
  - Confirm any pre-arranged accommodations and notify IT/facilities.
  - Provide a tailored onboarding plan that indicates adjusted timelines and key milestones.
- Day 1–14:
  - Assign a buddy who has completed the accessibility awareness primer.
  - Ensure all tools (Slack, Zoom, Confluence, HRIS) are configured with requested accessibility settings.
- Day 15–60:
  - Manager conducts weekly check-ins focused on workload, tools, and accommodations effectiveness.
- Day 61–90:
  - Formal onboarding review: People Ops, manager, and new joiner confirm any ongoing adjustments and update role expectations if needed.

Adjusting benefits and perks for equity
- Parental, caregiver, and medical leaves: People Ops will work with Benefits & Legal to provide options (e.g., flexible top-up, gradual return).
- Stipends and reimbursements: employees with approved accommodations may be eligible for higher or accelerated expense reimbursements for assistive technologies (approval via People Ops).
- Wellness and therapy benefits: confidential referrals and coverage details are available; claims assistance provided upon request.
- Commuter and travel support: alternate travel allowances for accessibility-friendly transportation can be requested.

Roles and career ladder considerations
- Performance assessments should focus on core outcomes and impact, not on differences in process or tooling. Managers must document objective evidence of contribution when making rating decisions.
- Promotion and calibration: People Ops participates in calibration cycles to ensure accommodations do not bias role-leveling. Any adjustments to timelines (e.g., extended ramp) are recorded and normalized across calibration committees.
- Role changes and lateral moves: discuss with People Ops to ensure interviews and transfers are accessible (e.g., alternative interview formats, extended timelines).

Internal tools and accessibility controls
- Supported tools and settings available by default:
  - Slack: recommended accessibility settings guide; keyboard shortcuts; reduced motion.
  - Zoom: automatic live captioning and recording transcripts enabled where consented.
  - Confluence: recommended fonts and structure for readable documentation.
  - IDE and terminal: company‑curated dotfiles and theming for high contrast and font adjustments.
- IT provisioning checklist (sample):
  1. Confirm OS-level assistive settings enabled (macOS VoiceOver, Windows Narrator, etc.).
  2. Install and license required assistive software.
  3. Validate VPN and remote desktop settings for low-latency remote access.

Manager checklist: immediate actions on accommodation disclosure
1. Listen and acknowledge; do not require medical proof up front.
2. Contact People Ops within 24 hours to start intake.
3. Adjust immediate expectations (deadlines, meetings) as an interim measure.
4. Ensure confidentiality and document the interactive process in private HR notes only.

SLOs and escalation paths
- Acknowledgement: 48 business hours.
- Initial plan proposal: within 14 calendar days of intake.
- Major vendor/ procurement timelines: communicated in writing within 10 business days.
- Escalation: if a request is not progressing, escalate to Senior People Ops (people-ops-lead@redwood.com) and to Legal for compliance support.

Data handling and confidentiality
- Accommodation documents, medical notes, and sensitive communications are stored in the HRIS restricted folder with access limited to People Ops, Legal (as needed), and the manager (on a need-to-know basis).
- Any requests for data deletion or retention exceptions are handled per Redwood’s data retention policy and local laws.

Metrics and continuous improvement
- Quarterly KPIs to track:
  - Average acknowledgement time (target: 48 business hours).
  - Median time to implemented accommodation (target: 14 calendar days for low‑complexity items).
  - Satisfaction score from employees post-implementation (target: >= 85% positive).
  - Representation metrics for roles across levels (tracked in anonymized, aggregated form).

FAQ (selected)
Q: Do I need to disclose a diagnosis?
A: No. You may disclose only what you are comfortable with. We may request limited documentation for long‑term or high‑cost accommodations, but this is handled confidentially.

Q: Will my accommodation request affect my career?
A: No. Accommodations are intended to enable performance. Managers and People Ops ensure that role expectations and evaluation criteria are adjusted fairly.

Q: What if my manager doesn’t respond?
A: Use the People Ops intake email (accommodations@redwood.com) or escalate to people-ops-lead@redwood.com. We maintain the SLOs above.

Example accommodation request template (email):
Subject: Accommodation request — [Your Name] — [Brief reason]
Body:
- Brief description of the challenge and how it impacts work tasks.
- Proposed accommodation(s) and preferred timeline.
- Any vendor or procurement needs (e.g., specific assistive software).
